uncited: **Identify Boundary Faces:** For every active voxel, check its 6 neighbors.
If a neighbor is inactive, record the shared face as a boundary face.
**Connect VFVs:** At each juncture, connect the origin of a VFV to the tip of a VFV from a neighboring boundary face.
**Resolve Ambiguities (POAs):** A POA occurs when two active voxels share only a single edge (in 3D) or point (in 2D analog).
At a POA, 4 incoming and 4 outgoing VFVs exist.
Apply the chosen Connectivity Mode globally or locally to select the successor VFV.
**Form Cycles:** Replace connected VFV pairs with VESTA cycle vectors.
*   In *High* mode: Calculate the average point of all support points in the cycle.
Connect this average point to all vertices of the N-cycle to form triangles.
**Displace Support Points (Optional for Isosurfaces):** Move support points along their range vectors based on linear interpolation of field values to approximate the isosurface.
DICONEX (DIlated CONtour EXtraction) is the 2D analog of VESTA.
It constructs gap-free contours from binary image data by connecting Initial Contour Vectors (ICVs) into closed cycles.
ICVs are oriented pixel edges separating active from inactive pixels, with the active pixel to the left.
At Points of Ambiguity (POAs) where active pixels touch at a single point, DICONEX uses a "disconnect" mode (left turn, same pixel) or "connect" mode (right turn, different pixel) to resolve gaps.
*   **Time Complexity:** Linear with respect to the number of active voxels and boundary faces.
The marching variant is more memory-efficient than the original global processing.
*   **Memory Complexity:** Original VESTA requires large memory to process the entire dataset at once.
Marching VESTA reduces this by processing $2 \times 2 \times 2$ neighborhoods.
Minimizes redundant support points compared to MCA.
High resolution mode adds computational overhead for average point calculation.
VESTA was introduced by Schleiermacher in 2010/2011 as a robust alternative to Marching Cubes, inspired by the 2D DICONEX algorithm.
It has been applied to relativistic hydrodynamic simulations and X-ray microtomography data.
